section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces error management instructions, citing previous work by Frese et al. (1991) and Nordstrom, Wendland, & Williams (1998) on error training. It argues that error training, combined with error management instructions, leads to higher performance by developing better mental models and countering negative emotional effects of errors. The section concludes by proposing Hypothesis 1, stating that error training with error management instructions leads to higher performance than training without instructions or error-avoidant training, indicating that this article will present one new study to test this hypothesis.
